text: Does a Gaussian wave packet v(x,0)=4*exp(-(x+5)^2/2.25), u(x,0)=0 decompose into a soliton train (>=2 well-separated peaks with amplitude>=0.8) in v by T=6 under the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system on periodic domain [-15,15] Nx=256?

method: Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing (zero modes |k_idx|>Nx/3=85) + explicit classical RK4 over full coupled RHS
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 depth=3 synthesis validated Fourier+2/3-rule+RK4 as the stable stack at amp<=3 T=10 (binding wall=aliasing not stiffness); adopting same stack at dt=2e-4 which satisfies dispersive CFL dt*k_eff^3=1.13<2.83 with 2/3 dealiasing. Negative entries rule out: no-dealiasing (BKdV-S1 single, kb-kdv-noDealiasing: aliasing blow-up before t=0.5 and spurious peaks), IMEX-CN (kb-gardner-G4: blows up at amp=3; amp=4 is worse), and central FD (Gibbs/hyperbolic failures). BKdV-S6 viscosity warning is IC-specific to bore-like u0; our u0=0 case is not a bore.

rationale: Phenomenon target met: 12 peaks in v at T=6 with height>=0.8 (minimum amplitude 1.32, maximum 5.21); all peaks well-separated (min separation 1.41 in x units). Mass drift=0.0000% (well within 8% threshold). v is spectrally clean (edge_frac=9.83e-8 above 2/3 cutoff, effectively machine precision). 2/3 dealiasing correctly handled the aliasing that would otherwise cause blow-up (per BKdV-S1). u developed large amplitude (~13) and high TV (583) due to Burgers steepening, but this did not corrupt v's spectral structure. Run is all-finite throughout.
F1 shows phenomenon target is met: >=2 peaks with amplitude>=0.8 (we have 12), mass drift=0%. v is spectrally clean. Stopping early at iteration 1.
